newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Karachi bourse wants bidding for issue.
newsitem.headline: Karachi bourse wants bidding for issue.

text.p: The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) has urged the government to put the launch of a $150 million bond issue for Pakistan's state-run telecom utility up for competitive bidding, a KSE official said on Wednesday.

He said the KSE had written to the government arguing that seeking local and foreign bids would obtain the best terms and conditions for the launch of five-year notes exchangeable with shares of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL).

The official, who asked not to be named, said the caretaker government had in principle decided to issue the notes, but had set no date. He said the KSE had told the government that uncertainty about the issue was affecting PTCL share prices.
Japan's Nomura Securities has submitted a proposal, at Pakistan's request, on terms and conditions, a KSE dealer said.
The KSE letter said competitive bidding was important to protect the interests of many existing shareholders who had bought PTCL shares at 55 rupees per share.
PTCL shares rose 0.75 to 32.40 rupees after the first hour of trading at the Karachi bourse on Wednesday.
